Install Cookie Compliance on your platform

View raw markdown (for agents)

In short: the banner is one two-tag snippet that works on any site where you can place code in the <head>, whatever it is built with. What changes from platform to platform is where the snippet goes. Find your platform below for the exact spot, or use the general steps if it isn't listed.

The one rule #

Blocking works by execution order: the banner holds the recognised trackers that come after it, in regions whose rule requires consent first. So the snippet goes first on every page, in <head>, as plain synchronous tags (no async, defer or type="module"), above analytics, pixels and any tag manager.

Scripts you mark essential (data-hu-category="1") run straight away. Recognised trackers wait for the visitor's choice, in regions whose rule requires consent first. What runs before consent is your decision.

Platforms with a guide #

Each guide shows where the snippet goes and how to confirm it.

Platform Where the snippet goes Guide
WordPress Install the Cookie Compliance for WordPress plugin, which handles placement wordpress
Shopify First thing in <head> of layout/theme.liquid shopify
Next.js The document <head> of the root layout, as classic script tags nextjs
Nuxt app.head.script in nuxt.config.ts, kept synchronous nuxt
Astro The shared layout's <head>, with is:inline on every tag astro
Angular <head> of src/index.html angular
React or Vue (Vite) <head> of index.html, ahead of the module entry vite
SvelteKit src/app.html, above %sveltekit.head% sveltekit
Google Tag Manager <head>, above the GTM container gtm
Hugo The head partial or baseof.html your layouts render on every page, first hugo
Gatsby gatsby-ssr.js setHeadComponents with the snippet first, or a custom src/html.js gatsby
Docusaurus headTags in docusaurus.config.js, as two synchronous script entries docusaurus
Laravel Directly after <head> in the shared Blade layout, above @fonts and @vite laravel
Django First thing in <head> of the base template every page extends django
Rails Directly after <head> in app/views/layouts/application.html.erb rails
Drupal The theme's html.html.twig, first in <head> (or a small module with a low library weight) drupal
Joomla The template's index.php, first in <head> above the scripts include (or a system plugin) joomla
Ghost The theme's default.hbs, first in <head> above {{ghost_head}} ghost
PrestaShop The theme's _partials/head.tpl, at the very top (or a displayHeader module at position 1) prestashop
Magento Magento_Theme/templates/root.phtml in your theme, first inside <head> magento
Wix Settings → Custom Code, on all pages, placed in Head wix
Squarespace Code Injection → Header (a plan that includes code injection) squarespace
Webflow Site settings → Custom code → Head code, then publish webflow
Framer Site Settings → Custom Code, at the start of <head>, then publish framer
Static HTML or any other site you edit directly First thing in <head> on every page (or the shared header file) plain-html

Your platform isn't listed #

If you can put code in the <head> of every page, the plain HTML steps apply:

  1. Copy the live snippet from the dashboard (Integrations → Manual Integration), or with the MCP server connected call install.getSnippet. Paste it unchanged. No account yet? Sign up (free plan, no card).
  2. Paste it as the first thing inside <head>, on every page or in the shared header your pages include.
  3. Confirm it with verify-install: in a region whose rule requires consent first, no tracking cookies appear before the visitor chooses. It also explains what to expect with Google Consent Mode.

The banner works from any spot that comes first in <head>. Most site builders have a header or head-code field: use that one. If a platform offers only a footer or <body> code box, look for its header option, or a template where you can edit <head>. verify-install confirms the result. A coding agent that finds no head position should tell the site owner which options exist before installing.
